content.intro: Learn grouping records with group by in the context of aggregate functions and grouping. This lesson covers the supplied syllabus topic, demonstrates a representative MySQL example, and finishes with a verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Analytical queries define a row grain, compute metrics at that grain, and make ordering and tie behavior explicit. Aggregate queries collapse rows into groups; window functions calculate across related rows without collapsing the current row set.

content_blocks.title: Apply the idea
content_blocks.text: Calculate a small result by hand, run the grouped/windowed query, and check row grain, ties, and NULL behavior. Write down the expected result before running the snippet. Compare actual output with the reference, then try one normal case and one edge case.

content_blocks.code: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(amount) AS revenue, AVG(amount) AS average_order FROM (SELECT 'books' AS category, 30 AS amount UNION ALL SELECT 'books', 20 UNION ALL SELECT 'pens', 10) AS sales GROUP BY category HAVING SUM(amount) >= 30 ORDER BY revenue DESC;
content_blocks.expected_output: The books group has 2 rows, revenue 50 and average order 25; pens is excluded by HAVING.
